question: What is the primary mode of acquiring taeniasis in humans?

options.A: Ingesting undercooked meat containing larval cysts
options.C: Inhaling airborne spores from infected soil
options.D: Direct contact with human cutaneous lesions

explanation: Human intestinal taeniasis develops exclusively when a person consumes raw or improperly cooked beef or pork that harbors cystic larval forms. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T24#GNS313_U2_T24_h1)

question: Why is Taenia solium considered a greater public health concern than Taenia saginata?

options.A: It causes severe somatic tissue invasion outside the digestive tract
options.B: It grows significantly longer within the human intestinal lumen
options.C: It is completely resistant to standard oral antihelminthic drugs
options.D: It reproduces at a much faster rate inside the human host

explanation: Taenia solium larvae can migrate to the central nervous system and muscles, leading to cysticercosis, whereas Taenia saginata remains confined to the gut. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T24#GNS313_U2_T24_h1)

question: Which animal serves as the intermediate host for Taenia saginata?
explanation: Taenia saginata utilizes cattle as its intermediate host, acquiring the infection by grazing on vegetation contaminated with human feces. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T24#GNS313_U2_T24_h2)

question: What structure of the tapeworm allows it to firmly anchor itself inside the human small intestine?
explanation: The scolex is the head region of the tapeworm, equipped with hooks and suckers designed to anchor the parasite to the intestinal mucosa. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T24#GNS313_U2_T24_h2)

question: What agricultural practice most directly accelerates the transmission cycle of Taenia solium in rural settings?

options.A: Slaughtering livestock during the dry harmattan season
options.B: Using chemical fertilizers on vegetable crop farms
options.C: Keeping cattle in enclosed, concrete-floored feedlots
options.D: Allowing pigs to roam and scavenge near human waste

explanation: Free-range scavenging behavior exposes pigs directly to human feces containing tapeworm eggs, completing the intermediate stage of the life cycle. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T24#GNS313_U2_T24_h3)

question: Which factor is NOT a recognized contributor to community-level transmission of taeniasis?

options.A: Rigorous veterinary inspection of all abattoir meat
options.B: Lack of proper handwashing facilities after latrine use
options.C: Consumption of undercooked beef or pork dishes
options.D: Inadequate sanitation and open defecation practices

explanation: Thorough veterinary meat inspection actually prevents transmission by intercepting and condemning infected carcasses before they reach consumers. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T24#GNS313_U2_T24_h3)

question: What is a common physical sign that often prompts an otherwise asymptomatic patient to seek medical care for taeniasis?

options.A: Expelling a thick, gelatinous mucus plug from the throat
options.B: Noticing painless swelling of the superficial lymph nodes
options.C: Developing severe jaundice and right upper quadrant pain
options.D: Observing moving white proglottids in underwear or stool

explanation: Patients frequently discover their infection simply by seeing active, flat, white segments of the worm passing out of the rectum. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T24#GNS313_U2_T24_h4)

question: A patient presents with mild abdominal discomfort, chronic nausea, and unexpected weight loss, and reports seeing flat white segments in their stool. Which diagnosis is most likely?
explanation: The combination of vague gastrointestinal distress and the hallmark visualization of passed proglottids points directly to an adult tapeworm infection. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T24#GNS313_U2_T24_h4)

question: What limitation exists when examining Taenia eggs under a standard light microscope?

options.A: Stool samples contain no eggs until the third year of infection
options.B: Tapeworm eggs are too large to fit within the microscope field
options.C: The eggs dissolve completely during routine saline preparation
options.D: Eggs of Taenia saginata and Taenia solium look identical

explanation: Microscopic analysis of the ova cannot differentiate between the beef and pork tapeworm species because their eggs share the exact same morphology. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T24#GNS313_U2_T24_h5)

question: Which laboratory specimen characteristic is required to definitively distinguish between Taenia saginata and Taenia solium?

options.A: Presence of hemolytic enzymes found in serum immunoglobulins
options.B: Specific coloration of the ova under an ultraviolet light source
options.C: Total lipid concentration measured in a 24-hour stool collection
options.D: Uterine branch count within an intact gravid proglottid

explanation: Counting the lateral uterine branches in a mature proglottid allows laboratory scientists to accurately differentiate between the two primary human tapeworm species. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T24#GNS313_U2_T24_h5)

question: Which medication is most commonly prescribed as first-line treatment for intestinal taeniasis?
explanation: Praziquantel is highly effective at inducing paralysis and detachment of adult tapeworms from the intestinal mucosa. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T24#GNS313_U2_T24_h6)

question: How does niclosamide primarily eradicate the tapeworm from the human gastrointestinal tract?

options.A: Triggering an aggressive systemic human allergic reaction
options.B: Inhibiting mitochondrial energy production within the worm
options.C: Dissolving the outer chitinous shell through intense acidity
options.D: Binding directly to human mucosal receptors to block attachment

explanation: Niclosamide works locally by disrupting the parasite's ability to generate cellular energy, leading to its destruction and elimination in the stool. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T24#GNS313_U2_T24_h6)

question: What severe neurological condition can develop when Taenia solium larvae encyst in the human brain?
explanation: Neurocysticercosis occurs when Taenia solium larval cysts establish themselves within central nervous system tissue, frequently triggering seizures. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T24#GNS313_U2_T24_h7)

question: How does autoinfection with Taenia solium lead to somatic cysticercosis in a patient who already has an intestinal tapeworm?

options.A: Excessive multiplication of scoleces inside the appendix
options.B: Direct migration of adult worms through the stomach wall
options.C: Ingestion of shed eggs via fecal-oral contamination
options.D: Absorption of parasite toxins directly into the bloodstream

explanation: If a person with an adult Taenia solium worm accidentally ingests infectious eggs through poor hygiene, the larvae hatch and migrate into bodily tissues. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T24#GNS313_U2_T24_h7)

question: What is the most effective primary preventive nursing action against contracting taeniasis?

options.A: Ensuring beef and pork are cooked thoroughly before consumption
options.B: Boiling all drinking water until large rolling bubbles appear
options.C: Taking prophylactic antihelminthic tablets once every single month
options.D: Avoiding physical contact with domestic livestock and pets

explanation: Thorough cooking denatures tissue proteins and destroys any encysted larvae present in meat, completely preventing human infection. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T24#GNS313_U2_T24_h8)

question: Which collaborative measure is essential for community health nurses working to control taeniasis outbreaks in rural areas?

options.A: Partnering with veterinary authorities to enforce strict abattoir meat inspections
options.B: Establishing permanent quarantine compounds for all diagnosed human carriers
options.C: Replacing all traditional open-air markets with modern refrigeration units
options.D: Mandating the culling of every domestic pig within a fifty-kilometer radius

explanation: Veterinary collaboration ensures that infected animal carcasses are identified and condemned before reaching local food markets. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T24#GNS313_U2_T24_h8)
